slides.stem: If $x^2 = 49$, what is the sum of all solutions to the equation?

slides.body: $x^2 = 49$ has two solutions: $7$ and $-7$. They cancel, so the sum is $0$. Answering $7$ means the negative root never crossed your mind — and the SAT counts on exactly that.

slides.title: Even powers hide negative roots
slides.body:
Squaring erases signs, so $x^2 = 49$ is solved by both $7$ and $-7$. Any time you undo an even power, write $\pm$ before you write anything else.

On grid-ins and sum questions, the forgotten negative root is one of the most common lost points on the test.
